findings.claim: RECORD.md's field rule "`declared_consumes` repeats them in binding order" does not hold for the record pyto actually emits: for 13 of the 15 invocations in evidence/run-1/record.json, `inputs` carries bindings and `declared_consumes` is empty. The shared contract and the shipped pyto record state different things about the same field.
findings.evidence: RECORD.md:52-53 says `inputs` keeps the testimony spelling (`px:<address>` or `fn:<id>`) and `declared_consumes` repeats them in binding order. In the real record every invocation whose bindings are result refs has declared_consumes []: e.g. fit.all inputs {"split":"fn:split"} / declared_consumes []; score.all inputs {"model":"fn:fit.all","split":"fn:split"} / declared_consumes []; compare inputs six `fn:score.*` / declared_consumes []. Only `select` and `split`, whose bindings are `px:`, satisfy the clause. The cause is materialize.py:416, `declared_consumes = [f"px:{address}" for address in receipt.declared_consumes]` — pcr.py:120 Receipt.declared_consumes records declared Part reads only, so `fn:` bindings never reach the field. Lane B knows the behavior and works around it (adapters.js:327-331 unions `inputs` with `declared_consumes` in derivePartIndex; tick-viewer.js:185-193 appends the `fn:` rows separately; viewer/README.md:79 notes it), but the contract file both runtimes must speak exactly still states the opposite rule, so any other consumer reading RECORD.md:53 concludes those 13 invocations declared no consumption at all. The JS side cannot settle it by precedent: I checked all six emitted adapter records and no DiscStudio, ChessLab or Wumpus invocation ever produces an `fn:` binding — every binding they emit is `px:`, so "JS is the reference" leaves this case undefined and the document has to.
findings.required_fix: Make the two agree, without touching pcr.py. Either (a) build the field from the testimony bindings in materialize.py:416 — `declared_consumes = list(testimony.inputs.values())` — which loses nothing, since receipt.declared_consumes is exactly the `px:` subset of the bindings in the real record (verified for select and split, and empty wherever the px subset is empty); or (b) amend RECORD.md:52-53 to state the rule the record follows: `declared_consumes` is the producing runtime's declared Part reads, the `px:` bindings in binding order, and may omit the `fn:` result refs that `inputs` always carries. Whichever is chosen, pin it with a test over evidence/run-1/record.json and bring viewer/fixtures/pyto-value-kinds.json onto the same convention (see the minor finding).

findings.claim: The synthetic fixture declares `source.runtime` "pyto" but models a declared_consumes convention pyto.materialize never emits, so it cannot catch a regression in the real one and it disagrees with the sibling pyto fixture.
findings.evidence: In pyto-value-kinds.json, `fit.all` has declared_consumes ["fn:split"] and `score.all` ["fn:split","fn:fit.all"], while the same invocations in the real fixture pyto-grouped-ablation.json (byte-identical to evidence/run-1/record.json) have declared_consumes []. The file also carries a concrete repo commit sha (42f4a66) and version 0.1.0 in `source`, though viewer/README.md:163 declares it synthetic and re-`pcr`'d to ablation.grouped.value-kinds. It is the only fixture exercising `svg`, `png-data-url`, `text` and `omitted` (7 json / 1 svg / 1 png-data-url / 1 text / 1 omitted), so its shape is what the render and schema rules for those kinds are tested against.
findings.required_fix: Once the declared_consumes rule above is settled, rewrite this fixture's declared_consumes to that one convention so both pyto fixtures agree, and set `source.commit` to null (RECORD.md:65, missing fields are null) rather than a real sha that implies a run that never happened — or generate the fixture from a real pyto run whose values cover the four kinds, which would remove the question entirely.
